name: Plastic water bottle
recyclability: High – PET is the most widely recycled plastic curbside. Rinse and recycle with the cap on.
alternatives: Stainless steel or glass reusable bottle
plasticFootprint: Medium – avg. 9–25g of plastic per bottle; production uses ~2x the water it holds
microplasticRisk: High – bottled water contains far more microplastic particles than tap water; heat/sunlight increase shedding
environmentalImpact: Major contributor to ocean plastic; heavy use of fossil fuels and water in production
bestAction: Reuse a refillable bottle; recycle single-use bottles with the cap on
practicalTip: Refill at water fountains — many now have bottle-filling spouts

name: Plastic straw
recyclability: Low – too small/light for most sorting machines; rarely accepted curbside
alternatives: Stainless steel, glass, silicone, or bamboo straw
plasticFootprint: Low weight, but used for only minutes each time
microplasticRisk: Medium – breaks into fragments as it weathers
environmentalImpact: Common beach-cleanup item; can harm marine animals
bestAction: Skip the straw or bring a reusable one; treat single-use plastic as one-time use
practicalTip: If reused, rinse and dry it right away — it's only safe for about 1 day before bacteria builds up. A steel/glass straw lasts for years instead

name: Plastic grocery bag
recyclability: Low curbside – needs special store drop-off bins (most groceries have one)
alternatives: Reusable canvas/cotton tote
plasticFootprint: Low weight, but used on average ~12 minutes before disposal
microplasticRisk: Medium-High – shreds into microplastics in sun and wind
decompositionTime: ~20 years (much longer in landfill, away from sun/air)
environmentalImpact: Major litter item; can choke wildlife and clog storm drains
bestAction: Bring reusable totes; drop clean plastic bags at store recycling bins, not curbside
practicalTip: Keep a foldable tote in your backpack or car so you always have one

name: Sandwich / zip-top bag
recyclability: Low – not curbside; store drop-off only if clean and dry
alternatives: Reusable silicone bag, beeswax wrap, small container
plasticFootprint: Low weight but used daily for lunches/snacks
environmentalImpact: Common litter; easily blown away, can be swallowed by animals
bestAction: Switch to reusable silicone or cloth bags for lunches
practicalTip: A clean bag (no raw meat) can be rinsed and reused several times before it tears

name: Plastic utensils (fork/spoon/knife)
recyclability: Low – rarely accepted curbside due to small size and mixed materials
alternatives: Bamboo or metal reusable utensils / travel utensil set
plasticFootprint: Low weight, made for minutes of use
environmentalImpact: Common takeout waste that breaks into microplastics
bestAction: Say “no utensils needed” on takeout orders; carry a reusable set
practicalTip: Keep a compact bamboo utensil set in your bag or backpack

name: Styrofoam cup / container
recyclability: Very low – almost never accepted curbside; special drop-off only in some areas
alternatives: Reusable mug or paper-based compostable container
whereToGetAlternative: Reusable mug from any store; bring your own
plasticFootprint: Lightweight but petroleum-based and does not biodegrade
microplasticRisk: High – crumbles easily into tiny foam beads
environmentalImpact: Styrene is a possible carcinogen; breaks apart easily and is hard to clean up
bestAction: Avoid foam entirely; bring your own cup or container
practicalTip: Many coffee shops give a small discount for bringing your own mug

name: Plastic takeout container (clamshell)
recyclability: Limited – increasingly accepted, check local rules; must be rinsed
alternatives: Reusable container you bring from home
whereToGetAlternative: Bring your own; reuse what you already have
plasticFootprint: Medium weight, single use
environmentalImpact: Food residue often prevents recycling; common litter
bestAction: Rinse and recycle if accepted locally; reuse for food storage first
practicalTip: Wash a sturdy clamshell and reuse it for meal-prep storage before recycling

name: Produce bag (thin plastic)
recyclability: Low curbside; store drop-off bins only
alternatives: Reusable mesh produce bag
plasticFootprint: Very light, used briefly
environmentalImpact: Litter; wildlife entanglement risk
bestAction: Skip the bag for produce with skins (bananas, oranges) or bring mesh bags
practicalTip: Keep reusable mesh bags folded inside your tote bags

name: Bottle cap
recyclability: Medium – recyclable only if left ON the bottle; loose caps fall through sorting machines
alternatives: N/A – use a reusable bottle instead
plasticFootprint: Small, but one of the most common items found in ocean litter
microplasticRisk: High – frequently found on beaches; breaks into fragments
environmentalImpact: Often swallowed by seabirds and marine animals
bestAction: Twist the cap back onto the bottle before recycling – never recycle it loose
practicalTip: Always keep caps ON bottles when you toss them in the bin

name: Shampoo / detergent bottle
recyclability: High – HDPE is widely accepted curbside
alternatives: Shampoo/soap bar, refill station, concentrate pouch
plasticFootprint: Medium – larger bottle means more plastic mass
environmentalImpact: High-volume category of household plastic waste
bestAction: Recycle empty, rinsed bottles; consider bars or refills
practicalTip: Look for refill stations at natural grocery stores to reuse the same bottle for years

name: Snack / chip bag
recyclability: Very low – mixed materials, not curbside recyclable; needs a special program (e.g. TerraCycle)
alternatives: Buy in bulk; reusable snack pouch or container
whereToGetAlternative: Bulk bins at grocery stores; Amazon for pouches
plasticFootprint: Low weight, but very high volume of daily waste
environmentalImpact: Mixed materials make it nearly impossible to recycle; common litter
bestAction: Buy snacks in bulk; use reusable pouches instead
practicalTip: Look for a nearby TerraCycle or store drop-off program for chip bags

name: Cold drink cup
recyclability: Limited – depends on material and local rules; lid/straw usually not recyclable
alternatives: Reusable tumbler
plasticFootprint: Medium
environmentalImpact: Common takeout/festival litter
bestAction: Bring your own tumbler; separate lid and straw before recycling the cup
practicalTip: Many drink shops offer a discount for bringing a reusable cup

name: Coffee cup plastic lid
recyclability: Low – small size and mixed type, often not accepted
alternatives: Reusable travel mug with built-in lid
plasticFootprint: Small, but a very common daily item
environmentalImpact: Common litter around cafes
bestAction: Skip the lid if drinking in-store; bring a reusable mug
practicalTip: Ask baristas to skip the lid if you're staying to drink there

name: Plastic toothbrush
recyclability: Very low – mixed materials, not curbside recyclable
alternatives: Bamboo toothbrush; electric toothbrush with replaceable heads
plasticFootprint: Low weight, but replaced ~every 3 months
environmentalImpact: Billions discarded yearly worldwide, most end up in landfill or ocean
bestAction: Switch to a bamboo toothbrush; look for bristle mail-back recycling programs
practicalTip: Check the packaging — some brands offer toothbrush recycling by mail

name: Disposable razor
recyclability: Very low – mixed materials, not accepted curbside
alternatives: Safety razor with replaceable metal blades; electric razor
plasticFootprint: Low individually, high over repeated monthly replacement
environmentalImpact: Frequent landfill item; hard to separate materials for recycling
bestAction: Switch to a reusable safety razor
practicalTip: A metal safety razor blade lasts weeks and costs pennies to replace

name: Six-pack rings
recyclability: Low – rarely accepted curbside
alternatives: Cardboard/paperboard can carrier; reusable can holder
whereToGetAlternative: Look for brands using cardboard rings; buy loose cans
plasticFootprint: Low weight, but especially dangerous to wildlife
environmentalImpact: Notorious for entangling and injuring marine animals and birds
bestAction: Choose brands with cardboard rings; always cut plastic rings before disposal
practicalTip: If you ever find one, cut every loop before throwing it away to prevent animal entanglement

name: Bubble wrap / plastic packaging
recyclability: Low curbside; store drop-off (same bin as plastic bags) if clean
alternatives: Paper padding, biodegradable packing peanuts, or reuse it
plasticFootprint: Low weight, but high volume due to online shopping
environmentalImpact: Rising fast with e-commerce growth
bestAction: Reuse for your own packages before recycling at store drop-off
practicalTip: Save bubble wrap in a drawer — perfect for your next shipped gift or move

name: Plastic milk jug
recyclability: High – very widely recycled curbside
alternatives: Glass milk bottle (some dairies offer returnable glass); buy in bulk
whereToGetAlternative: Local dairies/farmers markets with glass returns
plasticFootprint: Medium-High – one of the largest plastic items in a kitchen
environmentalImpact: High volume, but also a high recycling rate compared to other plastics
bestAction: Recycle empty, rinsed jugs; look for local glass return programs
practicalTip: Rinse the jug so leftover milk doesn't contaminate the recycling batch

name: Yogurt cup
recyclability: Limited – depends on material and local program; rinse first
alternatives: Buy a large tub instead of individual cups; reusable containers
plasticFootprint: Low-Medium
environmentalImpact: High volume of small containers, often skipped due to size/food residue
bestAction: Rinse and check local recycling rules; buy larger tubs to cut down on cups
practicalTip: A big tub of yogurt makes far less plastic waste per serving than single cups

name: Cleaning product bottle
recyclability: High if HDPE (#2) – rinse before recycling
alternatives: Concentrate refill pouch, refill station, DIY cleaner
whereToGetAlternative: Refill/package-free stores; some grocery stores now have refill stations
plasticFootprint: Medium-High
environmentalImpact: High-volume household waste category
bestAction: Refill instead of rebuying; recycle if switching brands
practicalTip: Keep one sturdy spray bottle and refill it with concentrate instead of buying new
